question.text: In Bohr's atomic model, the electron is assumed to revolve in a circular orbit of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>∘</mo></mover><mo>.</mo></math> If the speed of electron is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> Then the current associated with the electron will be__________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi><mo>.</mo></math> [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi></math> as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="]" open=""><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
Time taken to revolve in circular orbit is T=2πω=2πrv=2×227×5×10-112.2×106=107×10-16 s

Now, current associated with the electron is I=eT=1.6×10-19107×10-16=1.12×10-3A
⇒I=1.12 mA
Hence, the current is 112×102 mA.
